races.name: Download The At The Races App Amateur Jockeys' Handicap

runners_data.name: Pleasant Man
runners_data.note: Front-runner with sustainable pace but on a losing run, needs to use tactical advantage of controlling tempo
runners_data.comment: Ran poorly at Lingfield on Tuesday and Sisterandbrother looks his yard's best chance
runners_data.spotlight: On a losing run and he beat only one in 11.5f Lingfield handicap ten days ago; not ruled out though if back on his A-game.

runners_data.name: Green Team
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good form with course winning experience, key pace angle with limited competition up front
runners_data.spotlight: A three-time winner (including over C&D) in 2025 for Ian Williams; in good nick for his present yard too, fourth of eight in 1m3f Southwell handicap eight days ago; not out of things.

runners_data.name: Arth's Gold
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with recent winning form but faces tactical disadvantage in pace-less race
runners_data.spotlight: Finally opened his account at Southwell in April and he followed it with a solid third of eight there eight days ago; ought to be thereabouts again.

runners_data.name: Relocal
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who switched yards, solid recent third but needs genuine pace to aim at
runners_data.spotlight: Scored at Chelmsford (1m5f) for Roger Varian in January; not disgraced for his new yard with third of six in 1m6f Yarmouth handicap nine days ago, so he's one to consider.

runners_data.name: Lenny's Spirit
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse and course winner returning from turf disappointment, 18 days since last run
runners_data.comment: Promising stable debut in March (1m2f, AW); return to turf a plus; one to consider
runners_data.spotlight: In good form on the AW at Lingfield this year until a below-par sixth on turf in 1m2f Windsor handicap 18 days ago; this course winner can bounce back here.

runners_data.name: I'd Go Maniac
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with course winning form, first-time cheekpieces worked last time and back up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner in November; got back on track in first-time cheekpieces when second of 13 in 1m2f Windsor handicap 18 days ago; can go well again back up in trip with the headgear retained.

runners_data.name: Jack Sparowe
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who broke losing run in blinkers last start, up 6lb but has winning momentum
runners_data.comment: On a losing run but well treated and the change of headgear could give him a lift
runners_data.spotlight: Blinkered when ending a lengthy losing sequence in good style at Yarmouth nine days ago, drawing clear last 1f; up 6lb but another bold showing is on the cards with headgear retained and good amateur Henry Callan up.

runners_data.name: Sisterandbrother
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who won this race in 2024, in great form with two wins from last three starts
runners_data.comment: Won at Doncaster this month and ran well at Southwell six days ago; now 2lb higher
runners_data.spotlight: Has made a bright start for his current yard and made it two wins from his last three runs in 1m4f handicap at Beverley two days ago; also took this in 2024, so he's a player under a 4lb penalty.

runners_data.name: Now Then Wendy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from hurdles after 27 days, question marks over current ability
runners_data.spotlight: A fair 1m4f AW winner for Hughie Morrison in 2023; seemed only poor over hurdles for Steph Cameron subsequently, pulled up at Uttoxeter 27 days ago; returns to this sphere for her new handler with something to prove.

runners_data.name: Someone's Wish
runners_data.note: Hold-up type switching from hurdles after 36 days away, fitness concerns likely
runners_data.spotlight: Course scorer (for Robert Eddery) in 2023; a fair winning hurdler/chaser for Gordon Elliott since but pulled up over hurdles at Perth last month on final run for yard; more needed for his new stable.

runners_data.name: Glitter Code
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in first-time blinkers for new yard, 36 days since last run creates fitness doubt
runners_data.spotlight: Remains winless but he shaped well in first-time blinkers for his new yard when second of eight in 8.5f handicap at Beverley last month; can go well again in retained headgear if his stamina holds out over this much longer trip.

runners_data.name: Beaune
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with good AW form but disappointed on turf return, back to favoured surface
runners_data.spotlight: In fine form on the AW in 2026, scoring twice over C&D in April; beat one back on turf at Bath last time but no surprise to see him get back on track here.

races.paceDynamic: Pleasant Man and Green Team are the only confirmed front-runners, but neither has genuine early pace which suggests a moderate tempo early. With ten hold-up horses including recent winners Sisterandbrother, Jack Sparowe, and Arth's Gold all needing to be wound up from the rear, this creates a tactical nightmare where everyone wants cover. The lack of genuine pace-setters means the leaders can dictate fractions and kick when they choose. This race shape strongly favours the prominent runners and those with tactical speed who can position close to the pace, as the hold-up brigade will find limited room and pace to aim at in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Two Dominate Field
scenarios.trigger: If Pleasant Man and Green Team are allowed to dictate a steady pace without pressure
scenarios.body: The leaders can time their kicks perfectly while the massed ranks of hold-up horses get in each other's way turning for home. Pleasant Man's class edge and Green Team's course form become decisive when they have first run on the field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens significantly in the final three furlongs creating gaps
scenarios.body: Jack Sparowe and Sisterandbrother can use their proven finishing kicks to mow down tiring leaders. The recent winners benefit from having that winning momentum and confidence when the race gets competitive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Speed Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up horses manages to get an ideal position tracking the leaders
scenarios.body: I'd Go Maniac or Lenny's Spirit can use their tactical pace to sit closer than usual and pounce. Their course experience becomes crucial in timing the decisive move before the back-markers can get involved.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too slow and get swamped by the entire field in a cavalry charge
scenarios.body: Arth's Gold and Relocal emerge from the pack with the strongest late kicks. The lack of early pace creates a messy sprint finish where class and a clean passage matter most.

watchPoints.text: Pleasant Man and Green Team must be monitored early - if they establish a soft lead unopposed they become extremely dangerous
Jack Sparowe in blinkers again after breaking his losing run - any market move suggests connections confident of following up
Sisterandbrother ran just two days ago at Beverley and defends this title, check for any signs of quick turnaround effects
I'd Go Maniac keeps the cheekpieces that worked last time and returns to his winning course and distance
Now Then Wendy and Someone's Wish are both returning from hurdles after lengthy breaks, watch for any market confidence

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Always Happy
runners_data.note: Front-runner with course experience and highest rating, though was beaten as odds-on favourite last time suggesting some vulnerability
runners_data.spotlight: Siyouni filly who got off to a winning start in 1m Southwell novice in March; beaten at odds-on but advanced her form when second of 12 under a penalty in 1m Lingfield novice 17 days ago; she holds very good form claims.

runners_data.name: Hollywell Stream
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from long break but Murphy booking and promising debut form suggest readiness to fire fresh
runners_data.spotlight: 13-2, promising neck second of six in maiden at Doncaster (7f, soft) on her debut in October; winner has gone in again since, so this Lope De Vega filly must enter calculations with Oisin Murphy in the saddle.

runners_data.name: Hatour
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who showed good late kick last time and represents powerful Gosden stable with strong recent form
runners_data.spotlight: Sioux Nation filly; has shaped with promise on both her runs, running on well late on when third of nine in 7f Lingfield novice on her return 17 days ago; this step up in trip promises to suit; player.

runners_data.name: Flagpole
runners_data.note: Another Gosden runner returning from break who shaped well on debut and likely improved for experience
runners_data.spotlight: 15-2, encouraging debut fourth of 14 in 1m Southwell novice in November; this Starspangledbanner filly seems sure to build on it after a break.

runners_data.name: Venetian Sky
runners_data.note: Prominent type who showed marked improvement last time and remains open to further progress for powerful Haggas yard
runners_data.spotlight: St Mark's Basilica filly who took a big step forward from her debut when a running-on third of six in 7f Yarmouth novice 29 days ago; she's open to further progress, especially over this longer distance.

runners_data.name: Moonlit Surf
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer still looking green but improved last time, though needs to find more to be competitive here
runners_data.spotlight: Oasis Dream filly; still looked green but improved when sixth of ten in 1m Windsor maiden 11 days ago; can do better still, especially once handicapping.

races.paceDynamic: Always Happy will take this field along from the front with minimal pressure, given the lack of other confirmed pace angles in this small field. Hollywell Stream and Venetian Sky may track her prominently but both have shown they can settle, while the hold-up horses Hatour, Flagpole and Moonlit Surf will likely be content to sit back in the rear half. The lack of pace pressure means Always Happy can dictate comfortable fractions before kicking clear, while the closers may find themselves with too much ground to make up on the all-weather surface. This race shape strongly favours the front-running Always Happy and any prominent racers who can track her into contention.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Always Happy Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Always Happy gets soft fractions on the lead without early pressure
scenarios.body: She can dictate throughout and prove hard to peg back in the straight, with her proven course form and higher rating telling. The hold-up horses will struggle to make up the ground on this surface against her controlled tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Hollywell Stream or Venetian Sky press Always Happy early for the lead
scenarios.body: The increased pace will set up the race for late-running types like Hatour and Flagpole who have shown they finish strongly. Always Happy may crack under pressure having been odds-on beaten last time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Fresh Returns Fire
scenarios.trigger: If the long-absent Hollywell Stream shows significant improvement after 217 days off
scenarios.body: Her class as a Lope De Vega filly from the Chapple-Hyam yard could see her take a big step forward second time out. Murphy's booking suggests confidence despite the layoff.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Gosden Surprise Package
scenarios.trigger: If either Hatour or Flagpole shows unexpected early pace to disrupt the predicted pattern
scenarios.body: The race becomes more truly run which would suit their finishing kicks, especially Hatour who ran on well last time. Both carry the powerful Gosden stable form behind them.

watchPoints.text: Always Happy may get too easy a lead with no obvious pace pressure, allowing her to dictate comfortable fractions
Hollywell Stream returning after 217 days could be rusty early but Murphy's presence suggests yard confidence
Hatour and Flagpole both represent the in-form Gosden stable whose runners often improve significantly for recent outings
Venetian Sky showed big improvement last time but steps up in distance for the first time
The small field and lack of pace may result in a slowly-run race that favours those who can travel and finish

races.name: Free Tips On attheraces.com Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Anad
runners_data.spotlight: 150,000euros yearling; fourth foal; State Of Rest half-sister to winners Miami Matrix (7f/7.5f including AW; RPR 90), Ob La Di (10.3f/12.3f; 89) and Baltic Fleet (1m1f 2yo; 88); dam French Listed-placed 1m2f/1m3f winner (95); powerful stable is 2-4 with 2yos on AW this year; interesting.

runners_data.name: Rosevannion
runners_data.spotlight: 82,000gns yearling; seventh foal; Zoustar half-sister to winners Saariselka (6f 2yo; RPR 89), Israaj (1m/1m1f including 2yo/dirt/KSA; 84) and Kohoof (Spanish 6f-1m); dam unraced half-sister to two sprint winners; trainer 18% with AW 2yos (five seasons); market check suggested.

runners_data.name: Zarakova
runners_data.spotlight: 190,000gns yearling by Zarak; first foal; dam Group-placed 5f 2yo winner (RPR 99), half-sister to Canadian 1m Grade 2 winner Elizabeth Way, out of 1m Group 1 winner; leading stable is 11% with AW 2yos (five seasons) but 1-3 with them this term; market check suggested.

runners_data.name: Mohaymenah
runners_data.spotlight: By Minzaal; first foal; dam 6f winner (including 2yo; RPR 93); 11-1 at Doncaster (6f, good to firm) four weeks ago when racing prominently before weakening; looked likely to be suited by this slightly longer trip; needs to take a good step up on that effort to be involved.

runners_data.name: Harlequin Sky
runners_data.comment: 20,000gns breeze-up 2yo; half-sister to six winners; one of two newcomers for the yard
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to six winners, the best being In The Breeze (1m2f/1m4f; RPR 91); backed at double-figure odds on debut, when green but keeping on well to be under 3l third at Yarmouth (5f, good) last week; promising start; step up in trip should suit; contender.

runners_data.name: Angel Sense
runners_data.comment: Promising second on Kempton debut last week and she should improve for the experience
runners_data.spotlight: Showed signs of greenness when a close second at Kempton (6f, Polytack) and when beaten a similar distance in third at Nottingham (6f, good; favourite) where she improved; not ruled out.

races.name: Free Race Replays On attheraces.com Handicap

runners_data.name: Comprador
runners_data.note: Prominent racer stepping up to 7f for the first time which should suit, consistent AW form but needs to find improvement
runners_data.comment: Third in his three qualifying runs; makes handicap debut for a yard in flying form
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent without progressing in four AW runs (6f) for Ed Walker this year; changed hands for 16,000gns last month; improvement for today's extra furlong is essential.

runners_data.name: Court Of Stars
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer but has tactical speed, won over C&D recently and looks progressive for Sangster
runners_data.spotlight: Had issues with the stalls as a 2yo but she has returned from a winter break as an improved performer, winning a 7f handicap at Kempton this month and failing narrowly over C&D 11 days ago; should still have more to offer; one of two live chances for Ollie Sangster.

runners_data.name: Enamorus
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits the likely pace, returning from 258-day break but Palmer runners often go well fresh
runners_data.spotlight: She didn't quite live up to market expectation in three turf runs as a 2yo but there were clear signs of encouragement with her three in-frame efforts; not obviously thrown in for this handicap/seasonal debut but the trainer is in form and Oisin Murphy is always a significant booking for the stable (57 wins and a further 63 second/third place finishes from 217 rides; level-stake profit of +37); market confidence would heighten interest.

runners_data.name: Night Mission
runners_data.note: Pure hold-up horse who needs strong pace to aim at, drops in class but struggled in recent handicaps
runners_data.spotlight: Second or third in his three runs in 2yo novice events (all 6f, good ground or slower); unplaced in two 6f handicaps this year but he drops in class today and his pedigree strongly suggests stepping up to 7f will help; finished behind Dublin Bay at Ascot last time but was racing away from the main action; well drawn and a return to more positive tactics could see him run a big race.

runners_data.name: Paranjape
runners_data.note: Sits prominently and has winning form at this track, form from last run working out reasonably well
runners_data.spotlight: 6f maiden win here last November; stayed on for second of 12 in a Southwell handicap last month (6f); that race is yet to throw up a subsequent winner (as of before racing on Thursday) and he himself has since failed to fire at Haydock; stamina not assured.

runners_data.name: Dublin Bay
runners_data.note: Natural leader with course form advantage, won his last start here and Ghiani knows him well
runners_data.spotlight: Improved for the switch to nurseries last summer, winning easily at Ffos Las and Doncaster (both 6f) before finishing off strongly for sixth in a much stronger race at York's Ebor meeting; better than ever when winning a C&D handicap in April and his subsequent fifth of 19 at Ascot was in a Class 4; could still rate higher; key player despite a wider draw than ideal.

runners_data.name: Horwich
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with excellent C&D record having won twice here previously, well handicapped after recent drop
runners_data.comment: Won twice over C&D for Clive Cox; has run moderately in handicaps for new yard.
runners_data.spotlight: Won his first two starts, both over C&D, when trained by Clive Cox; struggled initially in handicaps for Ruth Carr but having dropped 10lb in the weights there were more encouraging signs over C&D 11 days ago (nearly 2l behind Court Of Stars), travelling strongly but just tapped for speed early in the straight; another 2lb lower here and he now has something to build on.

runners_data.name: Wyle Cop
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with winning course form, struggled on turf but much better on this surface
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark in a 6f maiden here on his reappearance in March; fair third at Southwell later that month but his form has nosedived on turf (handled it fine as a 2yo) on his last two starts (both in cheekpieces which are absent today); hopes pinned on the step up to 7f and the return to AW sparking a revival.

runners_data.name: Inferno
runners_data.note: Another front runner adding to pace pressure, tongue-tie and blinkers first time may sharpen him up
runners_data.spotlight: No improvement for the switch to handicaps at Nottingham three weeks ago (8.3f, good), unable to land a blow; a tongue-tie and blinkers are now added but he is drawn wide and hasn't looked to be crying out for the drop to 7f.

runners_data.name: Chapman's Peak
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won twice at end of last season but has struggled in handicaps this year
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in both starts since returning last month; needs a resurgence
runners_data.spotlight: Ended 2025 with a pair of wins in Kempton nurseries (1m and 7f); he has struggled in two handicaps this time around, however, and comes here with a point to prove.

runners_data.name: Flyta
runners_data.note: Speed horse returning from 121-day break with tongue-tie fitted, needs to prove fitness but has early pace
runners_data.spotlight: She was not beaten far in a pair of Kempton fillies' maidens (1m and 7f) in January, improving for the addition of a tongue-tie; neither race appeals as strong form though and she looks up against it now handicapping from the widest stall.

races.paceDynamic: Dublin Bay, Flyta, and Inferno will ensure a strong gallop from the start in this 7f handicap. Dublin Bay has shown natural pace and will likely lead early, with Flyta and Inferno pressing close behind creating a genuine tempo. The sustained pace over 7f on this sharp track will stretch the field and test stamina reserves in the final furlong. This strong gallop will suit prominent racers and those with tactical speed who can sit close enough to strike, while pure hold-up horses may find themselves with too much to do against the clock.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Dublin Bay, Flyta and Inferno maintain a solid gallop throughout
scenarios.body: The strong early pace will string out the field and favour those racing prominently who can quicken when it matters. Horses like Court Of Stars and Comprador, who can sit handy and have tactical speed, will benefit from the setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If the three leaders go too hard early and tie up in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The strong early gallop will set things up perfectly for the closers who can come with a late rattle. Hold-up horses like Chapman's Peak and Night Mission will have the perfect target to aim at.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle
scenarios.trigger: If the pace setters are more restrained than expected creating a tactical affair
scenarios.body: Without the anticipated strong gallop, this becomes more about raw ability and tactical positioning in the final 2f. The more experienced handicappers with proven track form will have the edge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Dublin Bay or Flyta get an easy lead and control the tempo
scenarios.body: One of the leaders will get soft fractions early and have enough left to repel all challengers in the straight. The pace advantage will prove decisive on this sharp course.

watchPoints.text: Dublin Bay and Flyta could go too fast early if they clash for the lead, setting up the race for closers
Enamorus returning from 258 days off may need the run despite Palmer's good record with returning horses
Night Mission and Chapman's Peak will need the three leaders to maintain strong pace to get competitive positions
Inferno adding blinkers first time could be too keen early given his natural front-running tendencies
Court Of Stars showed improved form last time and represents the in-form Sangster yard with claims

races.name: Free Bets On attheraces.com Handicap

runners_data.name: True Promise
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong Tapeta form but faces crowded early conditions with Murphy needing to secure good position
runners_data.spotlight: Four wins on Tapeta elsewhere, at 5f-7f, all in 2024; has been involved in several tight finishes since December, including for Oisin Murphy at Kempton (6f) in April, and while he's been on much the same mark throughout, he's worth another go over a bare 5f; thereabouts.

runners_data.name: Alondra
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse perfectly suited to expected strong pace, excellent C&D record with two wins here in February
runners_data.spotlight: Has a good C&D record which includes two wins in February, and there wasn't much she could do about her latest defeat on this track, when third to one well ahead of his mark; down in grade and one to consider in first-time headgear.

runners_data.name: Hedge Fund
runners_data.note: Sole leader who will face immediate pressure from four prominent runners, needs to handle sustained early pace
runners_data.comment: Everything went wrong on his comeback and he's entitled to improve for that down 3lb
runners_data.spotlight: Won over 6f on this track as 2yo; winless since that season but he's shown enough to think he can be placed to advantage off a reduced mark; had a troubled start to the season at Beverley but it's too soon to write him off; hood refitted with cheekpieces added.

runners_data.name: Dark Kestrel
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse often slowly away, C&D winner who benefits from strong gallop but may need more than this trip
runners_data.comment: Beaten returned to turf last time; still three years since sole win in this sphere
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner whose five AW wins include two this year; often slowly away; has been running respectably off his lower turf mark of late but probably needs a bit more for the adding of a visor.

runners_data.name: Curious Rover
runners_data.note: Prominent runner struggling for form this term despite reduced mark, faces traffic issues in crowded early battle
runners_data.comment: Second here in 2025; 6lb below his last winning mark; has plenty in his favour
runners_data.spotlight: Useful 5f turf form in 2025 but his season slowed down later in the year and he's been below best, despite the reduced mark, this term; 0-3 on Newcastle AW but he did handle that Tapeta earlier in his career, so perhaps the switch to this track might pay off in first-time headgear.

runners_data.name: Spendmore Lane
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse despite sometimes leading, often slowly away but finished fast when winning here previously
runners_data.spotlight: Often leads but can be slowly away; took a steep rise in the weights for two 5f wins in early spring but she absorbed it and added another win, from the fast-finishing Ancient State, on Lingfield AW in April; another solid effort back on turf there 11 days ago; strong showing likely back at 5f on AW.

runners_data.name: Blue Force
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 46-day break, has won over C&D but form has declined since December
runners_data.comment: Finished race off well for 3rd at Wolverhampton nine days ago; 1lb lower today; considered
runners_data.spotlight: Has won on all three Tapeta tracks, most recently over C&D in December, not as good since and although he ran better back here in April, he found little at Newcastle next time; others more likely.

runners_data.name: Mick's Spirit
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with exceptional AW record but finished behind better horses at Lingfield last time
runners_data.spotlight: Cracking 8yo who has won two Polytrack races in every season for the last five years; however, he finished behind Spendmore Lane and Ancient State at Lingfield recently and the return to Tapeta looks a negative.

runners_data.name: Jojo Rabbit
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with four C&D wins but latest was in 2024, has struggled here off this sort of mark recently
runners_data.comment: Conditions no problem and he went close off this mark at Beverley ten days ago; well drawn
runners_data.spotlight: Four C&D wins but the latest was back in 2024 and he's struggled a bit here off this sort of mark in recent attempts; has been running well on turf of late, though, and he shouldn't be that far away.

runners_data.name: Ancient State
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with three recent 5f AW wins, looked ahead of mark before narrow defeat at Lingfield
runners_data.spotlight: Looked ahead of his mark in first three 5f wins on the AW, most recently at Southwell in March; missed a beat at the start and only just failed to reel in the more prominently ridden Spendmore Lane at Lingfield since; raised a further 3lb but still has potential.

races.paceDynamic: Hedge Fund is the sole confirmed leader but faces immediate pressure from four prominent runners (True Promise, Curious Rover, Blue Force, Mick's Spirit) who will crowd the early positions. This creates a fast pace scenario over 5f with sustained pressure throughout, as the prominent quartet jostle for position behind Hedge Fund. The hold-up horses (Alondra, Dark Kestrel, Spendmore Lane, Ancient State) get perfect pace-setting conditions to unleash finishing kicks. This race shape strongly favours the hold-up runners who can sit off the pace and benefit from the strong gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent quartet pressure Hedge Fund into a strong pace
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop sets up perfectly for closers who can sit off the pace and benefit from the collapse ahead. Alondra and Ancient State both have excellent recent AW form and thrive when unleashing late kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent runner survives pace
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent quartet can secure an uncontested position behind Hedge Fund
scenarios.body: True Promise or Mick's Spirit could benefit from tracking the pace rather than making it, allowing them to kick clear when the leader tires. Their class advantage shows in a sustained drive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hedge Fund steals it
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners fail to apply sustained early pressure
scenarios.body: Hedge Fund gets an easier lead than expected and can dictate terms to suit his front-running style. His reduced mark and Tom Marquand's tactical riding could exploit a more patient approach from behind.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent quartet cancel each other out in brutal early skirmishing
scenarios.body: The pace becomes stop-start with no sustained gallop, favouring horses who can quicken from any position rather than pure closers. This chaotic scenario opens the door for improving types with tactical speed.

watchPoints.text: True Promise, Curious Rover, Blue Force and Mick's Spirit all want prominent positions behind Hedge Fund creating traffic chaos
Dark Kestrel and Spendmore Lane are often slowly away which could compromise their chances in a strongly-run 5f race
Ancient State missed the break badly when narrowly beaten last time and cannot afford a repeat over this minimum trip
Hedge Fund faces his toughest pace test with four prominent runners ready to apply immediate pressure
Alondra has the best tactical position as a pure hold-up horse in a race likely to set up perfectly for closers

races.name: attheraces.com/marketmovers Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Baltic Fleet
runners_data.note: Recently gelded and returning to form but lacks natural pace to pressure the leader early
runners_data.spotlight: Narrowly landed a 1m1f maiden at Yarmouth last September and he ran to a similar level when second at Bath on his reappearance last month (1m2f, good); gelded prior to his handicap debut at York (1m4f) two weeks ago, a race in which he was never far away but looked a bit awkward under pressure; upped 2lb but not yet exposed; AW debut.

runners_data.name: Galilean Quality
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who stays well but may struggle to get competitive position behind uncontested leader
runners_data.spotlight: Rounded off his 2yo campaign with a game 1m2f win at Pontefract (soft), after which he was gelded; made all to beat his sole opponent in a Southwell match (1m4f) last month but he could manage only third behind that reopposing rival at Chester (a solid effort nevertheless) three weeks ago; still capable of better; trainer also saddles High Storm.

runners_data.name: High Storm
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with tactical advantage but 44 days off and disappointed as favourite last time at Newmarket
runners_data.spotlight: Disappointed as favourite in a 1m2f handicap at Newmarket last month but his earlier Doncaster win (1m2f, good to soft) was encouraging; promise on AW in February; should stay 1m4f and he is not fully exposed just yet; Karl Burke is also responsible for Galilean Quality.

runners_data.name: Mythical Bay
runners_data.note: Consistent AW performer but running style doesn't suit likely pace scenario with Oisin Murphy booking notable
runners_data.spotlight: Made heavy weather of it when landing a 9.4f novice here in January (2-5 favourite); better in form terms when second of eight in a Chester handicap three weeks ago (extended 1m4f, good; Galilean Quality third) but he looked a tricky ride in the straight, hanging both ways; has the ability to deal with a 3lb rise but there are reservations.

races.paceDynamic: High Storm appears the sole natural front-runner among these four prominent runners, likely to dictate terms from the start without pressure. Baltic Fleet, Galilean Quality and Mythical Bay all prefer racing handy rather than leading, creating a potential tactical dilemma as they'll need to sit closer than ideal. The lack of genuine pace-pressers should allow High Storm to control fractions and kick clear when ready. This setup strongly favours the leader High Storm, as the chasers will struggle to generate the tactical speed needed to reel in a horse allowed an easy lead over this extended distance.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: High Storm Controls All
scenarios.trigger: If High Storm gets an uncontested lead and dictates moderate fractions
scenarios.body: The Burke gelding can kick clear turning for home with the three prominent runners unable to generate enough tactical pace to close the gap. His Doncaster win proves he can make all when getting soft fractions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Galilean Quality Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely strong with multiple horses tracking closer
scenarios.body: Lee's mount can use his proven stamina edge to outlast rivals in the final furlong when the pace collapses. His Southwell success shows he stays this trip well when others weaken.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Baltic Fleet Times Run
scenarios.trigger: If Loughnane can secure an ideal tracking position behind High Storm
scenarios.body: The Boughey gelding can use his higher RPR rating to strike late when High Storm begins to tire. His Bath second suggests he's returning to form after the gelding operation.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Mythical Bay Grinds Through
scenarios.trigger: If Murphy decides to force the pace early and pressure High Storm
scenarios.body: The Balding runner could create enough pace to set up his own staying kick, using his proven AW form. However, this requires a significant tactical shift from his usual style.

watchPoints.text: High Storm building an unassailable lead through slow early fractions with no genuine pace pressure applied
Galilean Quality and Baltic Fleet both trying to track High Storm in the same prominent position creating traffic issues
Murphy making an uncharacteristic front-running move on Mythical Bay to disrupt the expected pace dynamic
High Storm showing any signs of freshness issues after 44-day break when asked to quicken turning for home
Baltic Fleet responding better to pressure after recent gelding operation compared to his Newmarket disappointment
